findings.claim: The Packed-unwrap logic ("a column's kind is its primitive if Packed, else the kind itself") is duplicated verbatim in two functions instead of defined once. If a third kind wrapper is ever added, both sites must be updated in lockstep or `column_subset` and `should_encode` silently disagree on which columns match.
findings.source: columnstore.py:53 `alias = col.kind.primitive if isinstance(col.kind, Packed) else col.kind` and columnstore.py:63 `kind = col.kind.primitive if isinstance(col.kind, Packed) else col.kind`
findings.remedy: Extract a single `_primitive_of(kind: str | Packed) -> str` helper and have both `column_subset` and `should_encode` call it, so the unwrap rule has one owner.

findings.claim: `markers_legacy` imports the underscore-prefixed `_MarkerForm` from `markers_native` to build its own `Derived`. The leading underscore signals a module-private implementation detail, but the class is in fact a cross-module shared constructor -- the naming misstates its own visibility contract.
findings.remedy: Rename `_MarkerForm` to a public name (e.g. `MarkerForm`) in markers_native.py since it is intentionally reused by markers_legacy, rather than importing a nominally-private symbol across module boundaries.

findings.claim: `QuietQueue` is declared and never referenced anywhere in either file -- not constructed, not passed to `Workspace`, not used by `child(at:)`. The comment concedes it is "not wired into any scoping path yet," i.e. it is speculative scaffolding kept for a future need that does not exist yet.
findings.source: workspace.swift:57-59 `// Reserved for a future default execution context; not wired into any\n// scoping path yet.\nactor QuietQueue {}`
findings.remedy: Delete `QuietQueue`. It passes the deletion test trivially (nothing depends on it); add an execution-context actor when a concrete caller actually needs one, not before.
